title.narrative: Transform social norms surrounding knowledge, attitudes and practices of FGMC
Examples of success strategies and stories for building stronger movements and transforming social norms

comment.narrative: We did not have a target value for this

>Working groups and committees including FGM/C survivors, former cutters and faith-based leaders have been set up to develop and implement advocacy and policy enactment strategies > A wide variety of awareness raising and advocacy campaigns such as community dialogues, radio broadcasting and print journalism, school and youth-friendly dialogues, peer groups and workshops, multi- sectoral workshops and digital and social media campaigns. These have increased public support for laws and policies outlawing FGM/C practices and in some cases, developed interest in and demand for alternative rites of passage. Success stories under these objectives include an initial training of advocates in Nigeria which has led to 348 instances of public advocacy initiatives and over 30 campaigns reaching 2,891 individuals with anti-FGM/C messaging. Meanwhile, in Somaliland, the first ever anti-FGC policy has been submitted for official consideration.

title.narrative: Strengthen the capacity and effectiveness of grassroots and civil society organisations (CSOs) working on FGM/C
Examples of activities of organisations that have strengthened the capacity and effectiveness of CSOs.

comment.narrative: We did not have a target value for this

Organisations have continued to implement activities which have strengthened the capacity and effectiveness of CSOs. This includes: - Engaging new CSO representatives in FGM/C prevention efforts - Supporting individuals who have received capacity building and training to embed newly acquired skills into routine practices - Organisational strengthening on accounting, advocacy, MEL, and fundraising approaches - Specialised training on detection and referral of FGM/C cases.
